newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Opposition claims victory in major Serbian towns.
newsitem.headline: Opposition claims victory in major Serbian towns.

text.p: Serbia's opposition on Monday claimed victories in major towns, including the capital Belgrade, in weekend municipal elections.
The opposition celebrated its wins over the ruling leftist coalition of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic with a rally of 20,000 people in the centre of the capital.
"We are here now, and we are here to stay," Vesna Pesic, leader of the Civil Alliance, told the crowd.
The Civil Alliance ran for the elections in coalition with the Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) and the Democratic Party (DS) as Zajedno (Together).

The municipal polls came two weeks after Milosevic's coalition scored a resounding victory in national elections -- its first big electoral test since the end of four years of war in former Yugoslavia.
But it conceded defeat in major towns in the municipal voting.
Ivica Dacic, spokesman for the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS), said the leftist coalition won in 134 municipalities out of 174 in Serbia. But none of the big towns was on his list.
"The left coalition has 25 out of 110 councillors in the Belgrade city assembly," he said.
"Belgrade is ours, and now belongs to all Belgraders," said DS spokesman Slobodan Vuksanovic.
"This is a victory for democratic Serbia," Vuk Draskovic, leader of the SPO, said.
In the national elections, Milosevic's coalition won about 40 percent of the vote to 21 per cent for Zajedno.

But in Sunday's municipal run-off -- covering 5,603 city council seats in municipalities where no candidate had managed to obtain a majority in the first round -- the opposition reversed that result by claiming victory in the 12 biggest Serbian towns.
As well as Belgrade, they included major industrial centres such as Nis, Kragujevac, Uzice, Kraljevo, Kikinda, Zrenjanin and Cacak, and Novi Sad, the provincial capital of Vojvodina.
In Belgrade a DS spokesman, quoting incomplete results, said Zajedno had won 70 seats, the SPS 23, the nationalist Radical Party 15, and the right-wing Democratic Party of Serbia two.
Loss of control of the Belgrade city parliament would be a blow to Milosevic and sources close to the government said the SPS leaders were "shattered" by election results.
However, political analysts said that national power would remain with Milosevic, who retains tight control over the police, the state-run media and the economy.
Draskovic said the authorities would try to annul the opposition's victory by proclaiming the municipal results invalid.
But Aleksandar Vulin, spokesman for the SPS coalition partner the Yugoslav United Left (JUL), gave the elections a clean bill of health.
"We are also very happy that the elections passed in a completely democratic atmosphere, that we have no serious objections from the polling stations," he told reporters.
